target_pattern: Differentiate emotional verb patterns: gustar/encantar/fascinar for things and activities, caer bien/mal for interpersonal non-romantic liking, and querer/amar for loving people and pets.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Using one like or love verb for all emotional contexts.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish selects different structures based on meaning: preference for things, social chemistry with people, and direct love.
target_pattern_formula: a X + le cae bien/mal + person
natural_examples: A Ana le gustan las fresas.
No me cae bien mi jefe.

controlled_recombination.instructions: Write each in Spanish using the best pattern (gustar, encantar/fascinar, caer bien/mal, querer/amar). No answer key until the end.
prompts_en: Luis and Carla love listening to music.
I do not like my boss (non-romantic).
We do not like our teacher (non-romantic).

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Me gusta el chocolate. -> make it stronger with encantar.
Base: Nos encanta viajar. -> make it negative.
Base: A María le gustan las flores. -> change to singular noun.
Base: A Juan le cae bien María. -> make it negative.
Base: No me cae bien mi jefe. -> make it affirmative.
Base: A Lucía le caen bien sus compañeros. -> change to singular person.
Base: Amo a mi familia. -> rewrite with querer.
Base: Te quiero. -> rewrite with amar.
Base: Me gustan los perros. -> change to activity (correr).
Base: A ellos les encanta el teatro. -> change to plural thing (las películas).
Base: No nos cae bien el gerente. -> change to plural managers.
Base: Carlos ama a Ana. -> turn into question.
Base: Me fascina la cultura japonesa. -> change to plural cultures.
Base: Les gustan los videojuegos. -> change to singular game.
Base: Juan y yo nos queremos. -> rewrite with amar.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the most natural pattern and write in Spanish.
prompts: I like coffee. (me gusta vs yo gusto)
I love coffee. (me encanta vs amo el café) daily preference context.
I like Juan non-romantic. (me cae bien Juan vs me gusta Juan)
I like Juan romantic. (me gusta Juan vs me cae bien Juan)
I love my parents. (amo or quiero a mis padres vs me encantan mis padres) familial love.
They like to travel. (les gusta viajar vs les gustan viajar)
My boss does not like me as a person. (a mi jefe no le caigo bien vs no le gusto)
I am fascinated by this topic. (me fascina este tema vs yo fascino este tema)
We do not get along with the owner. (no nos cae bien el dueño vs no nos gusta el dueño)
I love you. (te amo or te quiero vs me encantas) direct love statement.

guided_personal_writing.instructions: Write one Spanish sentence for each specific meaning.
prompts: You like coffee but love tea.
You love listening to music while working.
One coworker likes you non-romantically.
You do not get along with one manager.
You like your neighbors.
You love your family very much.
You love your pet.
You are fascinated by one topic.
Your team loves traveling for work.
You like one person romantically.
You do not like one person romantically.
Your friend loves Mexican food.
You love your city.
One classmate gets along well with everyone.
You and your partner or friend love each other.

prompts_en: She does not like me as a person.
I love him, but it is complicated.
I like her, but only as a friend.
Do you get along with your neighbors?
They love each other a lot.

common_errors.mistake: Using yo gusto for liking things

common_errors.why_it_happens: Infinitives are treated as plural nouns.

common_errors.mistake: Using me gusta Juan in non-romantic contexts
Using caer bien for romantic attraction
Forgetting personal a with querer or amar plus people or pets

common_errors.why_it_happens: Literal translation of I love this.

common_errors.mistake: Wrong indirect object pronoun with caer bien/mal
common_errors.why_it_happens: Experiencer and subject are reversed from English.

common_errors.mistake: Using direct object pronouns with gustar-like verbs
Dropping article in gustar noun phrases
